steps.title: Something new, something old
steps.body:
Two jobs this week, and both are about how fast you learn.

The new: reading gets faster only by reading new music. Ask your teacher for a tiny piece, eight bars you have never seen. Sight-read it slowly, once a sitting, and keep going through mistakes. Do not stop to fix; a sight-reader's job is to arrive at the end.

The old: play the season's pieces again, one per sitting. Notice how much faster they come back the second time. That is the point of coming back: a piece learned twice stays.

1. Sight-read the eight bars, slowly, without stopping. Count out loud if it helps.
2. Play one of the season's pieces, hard bars first if it needs it.
3. Finish with the piece you will play at the season recital next week.

Next week is the last showcase. Choose the two pieces now, and one four-note tune you could teach to someone younger.

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes for the eight new bars sight-read each sitting, a fresh set every time, alongside the season's pieces played once each.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: sight-read the eight new bars without stopping, then the piece from weeks 1 to 3
Sitting 2: the eight bars again, then the piece from weeks 5 to 7
Sitting 3: the eight bars again, then the piece from weeks 9 and 10
Sitting 4: the two recital pieces once through each, as if recording
A four-note tune chosen and played slowly, ready to teach

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Then, in the same take, sight-read the eight new bars once.
